_what_this_is: Population anchors for estimating how many channels exist that would pass
the filter. These are ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE figures from public reporting,
not measurements, and several are years old. They live in JSON rather than
in code so that when you find a better number you can replace it and see
Every figure has a band. Use the band, not the midpoint — the midpoint is
false precision and the band is the honest answer.
Nothing in this file was measured by this project. The measured numbers
live in data/build-report.json and are much smaller.

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.note: Total channel count is widely cited near 114 million, most of them dormant or empty. The tiers below are the ones with any audience at all.

twitch.label: Twitch
twitch.note: The only platform where the live enumeration endpoint lets you sanity-check the estimate against a real count. Roughly 80-100k channels are live at peak.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.note: The least knowable of the four. No public creator census, no third-party index worth trusting, and the follower distribution is far flatter than YouTube's. Treat these as the widest bands in the file.

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.note: Meta reports professional (Creator or Business) accounts in the hundreds of millions, but most have no audience. Only professional accounts can return insights at all, so they are the only ones this project could ever measure.

youtube.why: 10,000 quota units/day; ~3 to measure a channel, 100 per discovery search

twitch.why: no quota, 800 requests/min; live enumeration converges on the active population over days

tiktok.why: no endpoint for any creator but the connected one, short of the academic Research API

instagram.why: business_discovery is a lookup by a username you already hold, not a search
